messages:
inc-bot: [P1] ALERT — Dedicated pool node preempting (spot) — customer: lyra-enterprise — pool: ded-lyra-vpc-2 — node: node-7f3a — GPUs: 4 (A100)
inc-bot: PagerDuty: @oncall-sre -> page triggered (policy: ded-pool-preempt)
oncall-sre: Acked. I'm on it. Picking this up as primary.
alice.chen: saw increased error rate for lyra tokens ~1:30 UTC, nice catch by monitoring. Are requests failing or just degraded?
ben.mallory: most requests to lyra-vpc-2 are getting 5xx from runtime (evict path). Customer-facing latency spikes and a handful of aborted sessions.
drew_patel: @oncall-sre can we isolate the tenant and start draining the node? Want to avoid data-plane requests landing on the evicting host.
oncall-sre: Agreed. Will isolate node and add routing override to avoid pool slot. Doing in two steps: 1) mark node unsched, 2) drain active sessions.
oncall-sre: Running: `rictl node annotate node-7f3a state=unsched reason="spot-reclaim"`
inc-bot: Command executed by oncall-sre at 4295002482
ben.mallory: nice. After unsched, run a graceful drain to move live KV caches. Use `rictl drain-node` with `--wait` for active streams.
oncall-sre: Executing drain:```
rictl drain-node node-7f3a --pool ded-lyra-vpc-2 --grace-period 90 --wait
```
oncall-sre: Drain started 4295002500 — active streams: 18, prefix cache weight ~0.62
lyra_ops: seeing 502s from our side around same time. We're confirming which of our jobs retried. Notified our SREs.
sam_custsuccess: pinging Lyra OPS to say we're mitigating and will route them to fallback pool. Will update the account Slack thread.
ben.mallory: routing: enabling customer-specific fallback route to `ded-lyra-fallback` (compatible model variants) for requests matching tenant_id=lyra. This avoids a broad pool-scale failover.
alice.chen: On routing change: will that increase latency for Lyra? Fallback pool smaller.
ben.mallory: Slightly higher median latency (+18ms), but stable. We prefer safe route over serving errors.
drew_patel: Drain progress: 18 -> 7 -> 2 active streams. Start moving large KV shards first.
oncall-sre: Drain at 4295002550: active streams 0. Node evicted by cloud provider (spot reclaim) at 4295002558, but cached sessions drained cleanly. No split-brain on KV observed.
inc-bot: Event: cloud provider terminated instance 4295002558 — node-7f3a removed from host list
lyra_ops: thanks, we saw the termination. Any persistent sessions lost? We had 2 long-lived ones — both retried automatically by our client and recovered.
ben.mallory: Customer impact assessment: ~1800 requests failed in 12m window, roughly 0.6% of Lyra's hourly traffic. No data leakage; all requests served or retried.
alice.chen: Post-mortem action items: (1) add preempt-notice hook to dispatch `rictl drain-node` automatically on provider two-minute notice if offered, (2) tune routing health checks for client retries, (3) offer Lyra a reserved node option for critical fleets.
lyra_ops: we'd like a dedicated reserved slot for our realtime lane. Can we get a quote and ETA?
sam_custsuccess: I'll loop in AE and account exec. Tentative quote process started.
drew_patel: For immediate stability, propose we offer Lyra an opt-in to `ded-lyra-fallback` as permanent (priority routing) until they convert to reserved. Need infra approval for capacity.
oncall-sre: Approve temporary priority routing for 24-72h. I've recorded change and throttles.
ben.mallory: Follow-up: found node host logged `spot_termination_notice` at 4295002460 — our detection took ~22s to surface. We should add 10s faster ingestion of host metadata.
alice.chen: Noted. Also want a playbook tweak: when evicting dedicated node for enterprise customer, auto-notify `custsuccess` and include tenant-impact estimate.
inc-bot: Action recorded: create incident ticket INC-2026-8742 and assign to oncall-sre; link: https://incidents.redwood.test/INC-2026-8742
lyra_ops: we'll schedule a maintenance window if they recommend moving critical jobs. Thanks for rapid response.
sam_custsuccess: Sent initial customer message: "We've routed your traffic to a healthy pool and are investigating. We'll follow up with options for reserved capacity."
ben.mallory: RMA: hardware provider indicates node termination due to spot reclaim, not hardware failure. Replacement is cloud-provisioned; restoring pool capacity to baseline in ~8m.
oncall-sre: Pool capacity back to baseline at 4295002660. Monitoring for residual errors.
drew_patel: Can we add a quick health-check script in the cluster agent to emit `spot_notice_seen` metric to Prometheus? That would let routing react earlier.
alice.chen: I'll add to backlog and aim for a short RFC this week.
inc-bot: Summary: incident contained, customer routed to fallback pool, graceful drain succeeded, node terminated by spot reclaim.
noncall-sre: Handoff: I'm handing to night oncall (drew_patel) for monitoring and follow-up; will update postmortem.
drew_patel: Ack and monitoring. Will open a follow-up thread with PM/infra for the reserved-fit proposal.
lyra_ops: appreciate the quick mitigation. We'll follow up with account team for reserved capacity.
sam_custsuccess: Closing customer loop now. Will update incident ticket with timeline and customer comms.
inc-bot: Incident status -> resolved (monitoring) at 4295002760
